tier_reason: py-pdf/benchmarks is an independent third-party suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, 337 stars) whose public harness (benchmark.py and pdf_benchmark/library_code.py) times pypdfium2 (PDFium) and the Poppler pdftotext tool on the same 14 PDFs on a stated CPU (Intel Core i7-6700HQ); compiler and flags are not stated (prebuilt pdfium-binaries build inside the pypdfium2 wheel, distro Poppler 24.02.0 binary), so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Text extraction average 0.1 s for pypdfium2 (PDFium) against 0.3 s for pdftotext (Poppler) in the README table (rounded to 0.1 s). From the suite's unrounded cache.json, the 14-document totals are 1.591 s for pypdfium2 against 4.008 s for pdftotext, about 2.5x (derived from page data), not 3x; per document the gap ranges from 1.36x (2201.00214, 0.535 s against 0.726 s) to 6.32x (2201.00069, 0.045 s against 0.285 s), geometric mean about 2.4x (derived from page data). README per-document rows: GeoTopo-book (117 pages) 0.2 s against 1.0 s, 1707.09725 (134 pages) 0.2 s against 0.8 s, 2201.00214 0.5 s against 0.7 s, 2201.00151 0.2 s against 0.3 s; pdftotext is never faster on any of the 14 documents (three ties after rounding, pypdfium2 ahead on all 14 in the raw seconds). Text-quality score 95% (pypdfium2) against 90% (pdftotext).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated: pypdfium2 5.13.0 is a prebuilt PyPI wheel bundling a PDFium binary from bblanchon/pdfium-binaries; pdftotext is the system /usr/bin/pdftotext binary, which the suite's HISTORY.md records as Poppler 24.02.0 (the README's '0.86.1' is a hard-coded label in benchmark.py, the version of the Python pdftotext package, which the harness does not call)
corrections.stars_or_usage: canonical repo on pdfium.googlesource.com (no star count); the read-only GitHub mirror chromium/pdfium (archived 2023-08-04) shows 541 stars; PDFium is the PDF engine of Chromium; bblanchon/pdfium-binaries tracks it with release chromium/8086 (PDFium 157.0.8086.0) on 2026-10-05, and pypdfium2 5.14.0 was released on PyPI on 2026-10-04
corrections.caveats: Independent suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, one script for every library, code public) but compiler and flags are not stated, so B not A. The README's 0.1 s against 0.3 s averages are rounded; the unrounded cache.json totals give about 2.5x, not 3x. Not a like-for-like harness: PDFium is driven in-process through the pypdfium2 ctypes binding (PdfDocument from bytes, get_textpage, get_text_range per page, plus Python post-processing that re-joins hyphenated words and adds page labels, which counts against PDFium), while Poppler is the /usr/bin/pdftotext executable run with subprocess after writing each PDF to a temp file, so Poppler's time includes process start and temp-file I/O; that overhead matters on the small documents (tens of milliseconds) but does not explain the large-document gaps (GeoTopo-book 0.238 s against 0.999 s). One run per document timed with time.time(), no warm-up or repeats; timings are cached in cache.json and only re-measured when an entry is cleared (the 2026-10-02 HISTORY.md entry reports no speed change for pypdfium2 4.30.1 to 5.13.0 or for pdftotext). The README labels pdftotext '0.86.1' while HISTORY.md says Poppler 24.02.0. The measured job is text extraction (content-stream parsing and text layout), not page rasterisation, so category rasterizers-2d is a best fit (the sibling MuPDF entry uses the same suite and category); PyMuPDF (MuPDF) ties PDFium at 0.1 s average (1.604 s against 1.591 s total). Licence: the LICENSE file in the chromium/pdfium mirror carries the BSD-3-Clause notice followed by the full Apache-2.0 text, and pypdfium2's README calls PDFium 'a BSD-style license'; pdfium.googlesource.com did not resolve from this environment, so the current upstream LICENSE and last_commit were not read (activity inferred from pdfium-binaries and pypdfium2 releases). Other PDFium-versus-Poppler rendering comparisons (PDF Association 2021 survey, Alfresco blog) were not read.

notes: Numbers match the py-pdf/benchmarks README rows; the 3x headline came from rounded averages and the raw cache.json gives about 2.5x, now corrected. Harness asymmetry (Poppler run as a subprocess with a temp file, PDFium in-process with Python post-processing) and single-run time.time() timing are documented; baseline_in_list true depends on the Poppler record in this same batch being kept.

tier_reason: Same independent py-pdf/benchmarks suite: public harness (benchmark.py, pdf_benchmark/library_code.py), stated CPU (Intel Core i7-6700HQ), Poppler's pdftotext timed against pdfminer.six, pypdf and pdfplumber on the same 14 PDFs; compiler and flags of the distro Poppler 24.02.0 binary are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Text extraction average 0.3 s for pdftotext (Poppler) against 5.5 s for pdfminer.six, 3.3 s for pypdf and 8.6 s for pdfplumber in the README table (rounded to 0.1 s). From the unrounded cache.json, the 14-document totals give about 19x against pdfminer.six (76.5 s against 4.008 s), about 11.7x against pypdf and about 30x against pdfplumber (derived from page data); per document the gain over pdfminer.six ranges from 3.5x to 47x (2201.00214, 0.726 s against 34.273 s), geometric mean about 13x (derived from page data). README per-document rows: GeoTopo-book (117 pages) 1.0 s against 14.0 s for pdfminer.six; 2201.00214 0.7 s against 34.3 s; 1707.09725 (134 pages) 0.8 s against 5.4 s. Text-quality score 90% for pdftotext against 88% (pdfminer.six) and 95% (pypdf). In the same table pdftotext is about 2.5x slower than pypdfium2 (PDFium) and PyMuPDF (MuPDF), and slower than Tika (0.2 s average).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: not stated: pdftotext is the system /usr/bin/pdftotext binary, recorded in the suite's HISTORY.md as Poppler 24.02.0 (a distribution build); the README's '0.86.1' is a hard-coded label for the Python pdftotext package, which the harness does not call; pdfminer.six 20260107, pypdf 6.19.0, pdfplumber 0.11.10
corrections.caveats: The headline wins are over pure-Python libraries, a weak baseline that is not a C or C++ incumbent, and Poppler is not the fastest engine in the same table: pypdfium2 (PDFium) and PyMuPDF (MuPDF) are both about 2.5x faster on the unrounded totals (1.591 s and 1.604 s against 4.008 s), and Tika averages 0.2 s; Poppler is in effect the incumbent that the PDFium and MuPDF entries beat. Independent suite (py-pdf organisation, BSD-3-Clause, code public; the organisation maintains pypdf, one of the baselines) but compiler and flags not stated, so B not A. The Poppler number is the pdftotext executable launched with subprocess after writing each PDF to a temp file, so it includes process start and temp-file I/O and does not measure in-process libpoppler speed (the README's libpoppler-cpp dependency and '0.86.1' label describe the Python pdftotext package, which is not used; HISTORY.md says Poppler 24.02.0). One run per document timed with time.time(), no warm-up or repeats, times rounded to 0.1 s in the README (raw seconds in cache.json, re-measured only when a cache entry is cleared). Measured job is text extraction, not rasterisation, so category rasterizers-2d is a best fit. Licence taken from the list tag and not verified: poppler.freedesktop.org and gitlab.freedesktop.org do not resolve here and the github.com/freedesktop/poppler mirror returns 404, so last_commit and stars are unknown. Maintenance inferred from search snippets only (Debian tracker shows poppler 26.07.0 uploaded to experimental on 2026-07-23 and a Debian security entry naming 26.09.0 as a fix version), not from an opened page. Rendering comparisons against MuPDF, PDFium and Ghostscript (PDF Association 2021 survey, Alfresco blog) were not readable.

notes: Numbers match the README rows and cache.json; ratios against pure-Python extractors are slightly understated in the record (19x, 11.7x, 30x on unrounded totals). Keep with shortcomings: the only measured win is over pure-Python libraries, Poppler is about 2.5x slower than PDFium and MuPDF in the same table, and the timed path is the pdftotext CLI including process start; licence, last_commit and stars could not be checked (freedesktop hosts unreachable).
